text:
lucy: Customer reported CSV download from Dashboard returns only header row when time range > 60 days and 'Include event metadata' is checked. They attach a .csv that is 154 bytes. Windows Excel just shows header and then gibberish or fails to open.

mike: thx, can you drop the job id / presigned link?

lucy: job id: export_2026_03_15_7732, presigned: https://s3.redwood-inference.example/exports/export_7732.csv?sig=REDACTED (expires in 2h). file size: 154 bytes. user locale: en-US, Excel 2019 on Win10.

arjun: quick hypothesis: we recently added gzip for large-range exports (>60d) to save bandwidth. suspect Content-Encoding header not set on the presigned URL or browser saves compressed bytes as .csv. Excel will show weird chars. can you confirm content-type + content-encoding from S3 metadata?

lucy: I checked via aws cli head-object:

```
aws s3api head-object --bucket exports --key export_7732.csv
{
  "ContentLength": 154,
  "ContentType": "text/csv",
  "ContentEncoding": null,
  "Metadata": {}
}
```

mike: aha ContentEncoding is null — that matches hypothesis. why did the exporter gzip the payload but not set header?

export-bot: export-service started job export_2026_03_15_7732 (range=90d, include_metadata=true)
export-bot: step=generate-csv completed, step=upload-s3 started
export-bot: artifact uploaded to s3://exports/export_7732.csv (gzipped=true)

arjun: looks like upload path writes gzipped bytes but uses the original filename and text/csv content-type. bug in upload wrapper for large artifacts.

sara: customer impact? only Windows/Excel? mac Numbers or text editor will show binary too. but many enterprise users open in Excel and assume header-only. we should prioritize.

lucy: customer reporting for a paid account, blocked, asking ETA. escalated to enterprise support.

mike: repro on my end: I triggered export with 90d range on staging and downloaded file. `file` tool shows: "gzip compressed data" but file extension .csv. Chrome downloads .csv and saves gzipped bytes. Excel shows garbage.

mike: quick fix: set Content-Encoding: gzip when uploading to S3 so browser will auto-decompress. alternative: detect gzip and gunzip before upload so S3 object is plain text. which do we prefer?

arjun: long term should store raw csv (uncompressed) for small-to-medium exports and set proper headers for compressed artifacts. short term, server-side post-upload fix: when we detect gzipped=true and headers missing, set metadata ContentEncoding=gzip via copy-object. can patch export-service to set header on upload.

sara: communicate to CS: temp workaround for customer: right-click -> rename .csv to .gz and gunzip locally, or open with 7-zip. but need an immediate fix on platform.

lucy: I sent customer the manual unzip steps and a direct uncompressed artifact (we generated via staging run). customer confirmed they could open that. asking for timeline for platform fix.

mike: I'll open PR to export-service to ensure upload sets ContentEncoding when gzipping, and also to avoid using .csv extension for gzipped artifacts (use .csv.gz). will add migration job to fix recent uploads in last 24h where gzipped=true and header missing.

arjun: assign to eng-infra for deployment change, but export-service owns upload logic. tagging @mike for patch.

mike: created issue INF-4921 and draft PR. ETA for patch to canary tomorrow EOD PST, full rollout after smoke tests.

sara: good. pls add a short status update for the customer with expected rollback/mitigation steps.

lucy: will update customer and mark ticket P1. thanks all :thumbsup:

mike: one more note — add a regression test: head-object metadata must include ContentEncoding when gzipped flag is true. test added in PR.

arjun: also add an analytic event when export switches to gzip so we can track frequency.

lucy: closing loop: customer replied thanks and will re-open if anything else.

export-bot: export-service job export_2026_03_15_7732 status=resolved (manual workaround delivered)
